Feb 2021
-Analysis of admissions relating to substance misuse to support review of substance misuse services
-Analysis of admissions relating to childhood injury to support under 19 strategy
-Update of JSNA sections to identify areas of potential need in the district
-Analysis of admissions to support Community Partnership profiles to identify areas of need

Main pieces of work have involved:
- analysis of self harm admissions to support suicide audit
- update of JSNA to identify areas of potential need in the district

- Breakdown of elective, non-elective and A&E admission rates by CCG by deprivation quintile to inform CCG priorities / allocate resources across the CCGs.
texts.8ea9d9c825a1:
Main pieces of work have involved:
- analysis of unplanned admissions in 2011-12 and 2015-16 to support work around what the main contribution to these are to feedback to CCGs in order for them to reduce unplanned admissions in their relevant areas
- update of JSNA to identify areas of potential need in the district
- Breakdown of elective, non-elective and a&E admission rates by CCG by deprivation quintile to inform CCG priorities / allocate resources across the CCGs

texts.f4cd0850a0c1:
Access to the data will enable the Local Authority to undertake locally-focused and locally-responsive analyses of health status and health outcomes. For example, the data will be used to produce analyses of health inequalities for non-standard geographies and for specific social or ethnic groups in the local population to help ensure that the health challenges facing the local population – particularly the most disadvantaged – have been identified and responded to appropriately by the Local Authority and its partners.

It is recognised that in fulfilling its public health duties using HES data, the Local Authority will deliver significant benefits. The Local Authority therefore commits in any renewal request to providing additional detail on benefits that relate to their local use of the data.
